name: Arapaho Peaks Traverse

pitch_detail.notes: Arapaho Pass trail to the mine ruins, Arapaho Glacier trail to the saddle, then a loose rocky scramble past a false summit to the top.
Leave South Arapaho northward; an exposed downclimb of about 50 ft, then sustained blocky scrambling. Stay near the crest, escape west at difficulties.
About three quarters of the way along: two short steps of roughly 8-10 ft each on good holds, above exposure.
Easier ground, sometimes a snow patch, to the broad summit.
Reverse the ridge back to South Arapaho; the crux steps are downclimbed.
Scramble off South Arapaho and follow the trails back down.

descent_text: Reverse the traverse south to South Arapaho, then descend the Arapaho Glacier trail and Arapaho Pass trail back to the trailhead. Descending the east side of the ridge toward the glacier is not an option: that basin is closed to all entry.
approach: From the Fourth of July Trailhead, take the Arapaho Pass trail past the Diamond Lake junction (about 1.1 mi) to the Fourth of July Mine ruins (about 2 mi). Turn sharply back to the northeast onto the signed Arapaho Glacier trail and follow it above treeline to the saddle on South Arapaho's southeast shoulder (about 12,700 ft), then scramble to South Arapaho's summit (about 4 mi from the trailhead).
overview: A classic ridge scramble linking the two Arapaho Peaks, finishing on North Arapaho, the highest summit in the Indian Peaks. A good trail leads to South Arapaho, then a sustained, exposed Class 3 ridge with a brief Class 4 crux leads north above the Arapaho Glacier. Most parties return the same way, back over South Arapaho.
beta: Trail to South Arapaho: follow the Arapaho Pass trail to the Fourth of July Mine ruins, then switch back northeast on the signed Arapaho Glacier trail. It climbs steadily above treeline to the saddle southeast of South Arapaho, where the trail ends and a rocky, loose Class 2 scramble past a false summit leads to the top. The traverse: from South Arapaho's summit, follow the connecting ridge north, about three quarters of a mile one way. Almost all of it is Class 3, with roughly 300 ft of downclimbing and 400 ft of climbing each way, including a somewhat exposed Class 3 downclimb of about 50 ft early on. Stay near the crest and escape to the west side at difficulties; the east side drops to the glacier. Occasional painted marks and cairns show the line but are sparse. The crux: about three quarters of the way to North Arapaho, two short steps of roughly 8-10 ft each go at Class 4 on good holds; some parties find a line that stays Class 3. Final slopes: easier ground, sometimes with a lingering snow patch, leads to North Arapaho's broad summit. Allow at least an hour each way on the ridge.
